topic.readerProblem: A founder or marketer sees ChatGPT state outdated facts about their company and wants to know how often ChatGPT updates, whether live search saves them, and what to change first.
topic.connection: Separates ChatGPT's frozen training memory from live retrieval so AEOeye readers fix the pages and crawler access that AI engines can actually fetch, and check results with a repeatable with-search / without-search test.

assessment: The page answers the cutoff-versus-live-search question with OpenAI's own dated model pages and changelog (cutoffs from Aug 31, 2025 to May 18, 2026; four models released Sep 3-29, 2026), explains that the model behind ChatGPT's Instant chat has an older cutoff than the flagships, and ties retrieval to a 2026 arXiv chatbot test and to AEOeye's crawler access study with its limits. It deliberately does not state a fixed refresh schedule for ChatGPT, a recrawl frequency for content, how many pages ChatGPT reads, or how repetition is weighted in current training data, because OpenAI publishes none of these; the weighting point is labelled as our reading.

sources.supports: Knowledge cutoffs: GPT-6 Astra Apr 30, 2026; GPT-6.1 Sol Apr 30, 2026; GPT-6 Luna May 18, 2026 (confirmed in the raw page text).
chat-latest 'points to the latest Instant model currently used in ChatGPT', 'Aug 31, 2025 knowledge cutoff', snapshot 'will be regularly updated' (confirmed in raw HTML).
Release dates: GPT-6 Astra Sep 3, GPT-6 Sol and Luna Sep 22, GPT-6.1 Sol Sep 29 (2026 sections); chat-latest snapshots May 5 and May 28, 2026 (confirmed in raw page text).

The model can choose to search the web or not based on the prompt; three search types (non-reasoning, agentic, deep research 'often tapping into hundreds of sources'); inline citations by default (confirmed in raw HTML).

OAI-SearchBot: opted-out sites 'will not be shown in ChatGPT search answers, though can still appear as navigational links'; OpenAI recommends allowing it; ~24 hours for robots.txt updates to take effect in search; ChatGPT-User robots.txt rules may not apply (confirmed in raw HTML).

Suzgun et al.: fourteen-day (Feb 9-22, 2026) evaluation of six chatbots on 2,100 same-day BBC-derived questions; best systems over 90% multiple-choice accuracy; retrieval failures drive over 70% of errors (abstract confirmed in the downloaded PDF text).
Definition of RAG as a technique that enables LLMs to retrieve and incorporate new information from external data sources.
